content:
# Welcome

## How this app works

This is the hands-on companion for DSI training sessions. The **Data**
tab loads your dataset (or the built-in cat-café example); the
**Missing data** and **Outliers** tabs let you practise the cleaning
steps from the slides.

Every file in the `lessons/` folder appears as a tab like this one —
facilitators add session-specific instructions by dropping in a
markdown file, no code changes needed.

## Ground rules

- Understand your data. Understand what you want.
- Inspect before you impute.
- One chart, one message, one action.

name: lessons/02-exercise-cats.md
content:
# Exercise: the cat café

Load the example data on the **Data** tab, then:

1. **Diagnose** — how many rows, columns, missing values? Which variables
   look wrong? (Hint: check `summary()` output in the Structure panel —
   a 5 cm cat and a 56 kg cat live in this table.)
2. **Missing data** — open the *Missing data* tab. Which variable has
   gaps? Inspect the pattern first, then choose an imputation method and
   justify it.
3. **Outliers** — open the *Outliers* tab. Boxplot `weight_kg`. Should the
   extreme value be corrected, winsorized, or kept?
4. **Discuss** — in one sentence: what would you tell the café owner
   about what makes a cat playful?

Time: 20 minutes hands-on, 10 minutes discussion.

name: teaching-helpers.R
content:
# teaching-helpers.R -----------------------------------------------------
# Consolidated helper functions used across the training modules.
# Source this file at the top of any training deck or exercise script:
#   source("../shared/R/teaching-helpers.R")
#
# Origins (kept verbatim where possible):
#   - geomean / weighted_geomean / dtable: 2025-11-18-lecture (R/load.R)
#   - ggpie / gghist: 2025-06-17-DHP-session lesson 01
#   - has_missing / recognize_outlier / winsorize / catatable:
#     2025-07-22-ghlc-course and 2025-08-12-cata-science (R/app-function.R)

library(tidyverse)
library(cowplot)
library(DT)
library(naniar)
library(mice)


# Aggregation -------------------------------------------------------------

# Geometric mean (values must be positive). Used to teach UHC SCI
# aggregation. For production analysis prefer DSIR::geomean().
geomean <- function(x) {
  stopifnot(all(x > 0, na.rm = TRUE))
  exp(mean(log(x), na.rm = TRUE))
}

# Weighted geometric mean, the 2025-revision method for within-domain
# aggregation of UHC SCI tracers (w = tracer denominator population).
weighted_geomean <- function(x, w) {
  stopifnot(all(x > 0, na.rm = TRUE))
  exp(weighted.mean(log(x), w, na.rm = TRUE))
}


# Missing data ------------------------------------------------------------

# Friendly missingness summary for live demos.
has_missing <- function(df) {
  if (any_miss(df)) {
    cat(
      "There is still missing data...\n",
      n_miss(df), " values missing,\n",
      n_var_miss(df), " variables with missing,\n",
      n_case_miss(df), " rows incomplete.\n"
    )
  } else {
    cat(capture.output(md.pattern(df, plot = FALSE))[1:6], sep = "\n")
  }
}


# Outliers ----------------------------------------------------------------

# IQR rule: returns TRUE for values inside [Q1 - k*IQR, Q3 + k*IQR].
recognize_outlier <- function(vec, k = 1.5) {
  if (!is.numeric(vec)) {
    return(cat("Please input a numeric vector.\n"))
  }
  q1 <- quantile(vec, .25, na.rm = TRUE)
  q3 <- quantile(vec, .75, na.rm = TRUE)
  iqr <- q3 - q1
  between(vec, q1 - k * iqr, q3 + k * iqr)
}

# Winsorize: cap values at the IQR fences instead of dropping them.
winsorize <- function(vec, k = 1.5) {
  if (!is.numeric(vec)) {
    return(cat("Please input a numeric vector.\n"))
  }
  q1 <- quantile(vec, .25, na.rm = TRUE)
  q3 <- quantile(vec, .75, na.rm = TRUE)
  iqr <- q3 - q1
  lower <- q1 - k * iqr
  upper <- q3 + k * iqr
  vec[vec > upper] <- upper
  vec[vec < lower] <- lower
  vec
}


# Tables ------------------------------------------------------------------

# Interactive table with copy/export buttons (for HTML decks and Shiny).
dtable <- function(df) {
  datatable(
    df,
    extensions = "Buttons",
    options = list(dom = "Bfrtip", buttons = c("copy", "csv", "excel"))
  )
}

# Scrollable variant for wide tables.
dtable1 <- function(df) {
  datatable(
    df,
    extensions = "Buttons",
    options = list(
      dom = "Bfrtip", buttons = c("copy", "csv", "excel"),
      scrollX = TRUE, scrollY = TRUE, pageLength = 9
    )
  )
}


# Quick EDA plots ---------------------------------------------------------

# Simple pie chart of one categorical column (teaching EDA only; for WHO
# deliverables prefer DSIR::ggpie() with theme_dsi()).
ggpie_simple <- function(df, column, offset = 1.3) {
  df_count <- df %>%
    count(.data[[column]]) %>%
    set_names("fact", "n") %>%
    mutate(
      perc = scales::percent(n / sum(n), accuracy = .1),
      label = paste0(fact, ": ", n, "\n(", perc, ")"),
      y = cumsum(n) - n / 2
    )
  ggplot(df_count, aes(1, n, fill = fct_rev(fact))) +
    geom_col(color = "white") +
    geom_text(aes(label = label, y = y, x = offset)) +
    coord_polar("y") +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
    theme_cowplot() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      axis.text = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks = element_blank(),
      axis.line = element_blank(),
      axis.title = element_blank()
    ) +
    ggtitle(paste0("Distribution of ", column))
}

# Simple histogram of one numeric column.
gghist <- function(df, column, .bins = 6) {
  ggplot(df, aes(.data[[column]])) +
    geom_histogram(color = "white", fill = "cadetblue", bins = .bins) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .04))) +
    labs(
      x = "", y = "Count",
      title = paste0("Distribution of ", column)
    )
}


# Toy data ----------------------------------------------------------------

# Synthetic patient data with two hidden clusters (young/healthy vs
# old/at-risk). Used in the AI-prompting module light-structure exercise.
make_patients <- function(n = 200, seed = 123) {
  set.seed(seed)
  data <- tibble(
    patient_id = 1:n,
    age = c(rnorm(n / 2, mean = 32, sd = 3), rnorm(n / 2, mean = 68, sd = 4)),
    systolic_bp = c(rnorm(n / 2, mean = 115, sd = 5), rnorm(n / 2, mean = 155, sd = 6)),
    cholesterol = c(rnorm(n / 2, mean = 175, sd = 10), rnorm(n / 2, mean = 260, sd = 12)),
    bmi = c(rnorm(n / 2, mean = 21, sd = 1.5), rnorm(n / 2, mean = 30, sd = 1.8))
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      systolic_bp = systolic_bp + rnorm(n, 0, 1.5),
      cholesterol = cholesterol + rnorm(n, 0, 3),
      bmi = pmax(18, pmin(36, bmi))
    )
  # shuffle rows so the cluster structure is hidden
  data[sample(nrow(data)), ]
}
